subject: Claude Physics Record 🔬, VoiceStudio 646-Language Cloning 🎙️, Anthropi
intro: Anthropic had a big week. Claude cracked a nine-loop physics record, mostly unsupervised, for under $2k. Then launched a plugin portal as MCP usage hits 110x growth. The pattern is clear: AI is moving from assistant to autonomous operator, whether in a physics lab or a developer ecosystem. The scaffolding is being built fast. Meanwhile, a new detector spots AI-written content with 98% accuracy using structure alone. Paraphrasing won't save you. The shape gives it away.

news.headline: Solo dev releases free open-source voice cloning tool supporting 646 languages
news.body: ElevenLabs charges per character and caps you at 32 languages. VoiceStudio just made that feel outdated. It's a free, open-source voice tool that runs 100% on your own machine . No cloud. No billing. Your audio never leaves your computer. Here's what you can do with it: To get started: git clone the repo, run bun install, then bun run setup:api and bun run dev. Node 20+ and Python 3.11+ are both required before you begin. One heads up: model licenses vary, so check them before any commercial use. And clone voices only with permission. The repo already has 37k stars. People are clearly paying attention.
bullets: Clone any voice from a short audio clip
Generate audiobooks, run dictation, and transcribe audio
Pick from 14 different text-to-speech engines instead of being locked to one

news.headline: Developer reverse-engineers a 2007 Nokia to run Claude with 8MB of RAM
news.body: Someone took a 2007 Nokia 6300 with 8 MB of RAM, and gave it an AI brain. Yes, really. The problem: old Nokia phones only speak an ancient version of HTTPS that every modern server rejects. So the solution was clever: build a small Go server that acts as a translator. The phone talks old-school to the server, the server talks modern HTTPS to Claude's API. Problem solved. What you can actually do on the phone: To run it yourself, you need a cheap VPS, Docker, and an old Series 40 Nokia . The full app, server, and setup guide are open source on GitHub at emir/claude-s40.
bullets: Chat with Claude using the physical keypad, with a typing indicator and chat history
Get live web search results, weather, and exchange rates
Add calendar entries by just asking Claude in plain text
Page through long replies in a reading mode

news.headline: Claude breaks physics world record by solving nine-loop particle calculation unsupervised
news.body: Physics just got a new record holder, and it's an AI. Here's the quick version. When particles collide, physicists use formulas called scattering amplitudes to predict what happens. Getting those formulas right requires adding layers of corrections called "loops." Each added loop makes the answer more precise but takes exponentially more computation. Most formulas have been calculated only to two loops, and a few to three. The previous record in this model sat at eight loops , set by Lance Dixon of SLAC and his collaborators. A physicist then publicly challenged AI labs to beat it on an academic budget. Anthropic ran Claude inside a harness called Claude Science, driving Python with SymPy across 96 CPUs for a week , at a total cost of roughly $1,000-$2,000 . One prompt. Mostly unsupervised. The result was personally verified by the creator of the eight-loop record. What this opens up: AI can now tackle frontier math problems that were stuck for years, at a cost any research team can afford.
